name: Yeniche
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Yeniche is a German-based in-group lexicon; sources found (Matras 'Jenisch'; Weinstein 2013) are lexical/sociolinguistic, no stress description.

sources.citation: de.wikipedia 'Jenische Sprache' (raw wikitext saved) and en.wikipedia 'Yenish language'
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Secondary: Jenisch keeps 'Grammatik, Syntax und Lautsystem' of the surrounding majority language; its literature list supplied the open Efing/Wittich links. English page cites Weinstein 2013 (not seen) for 'syntax borrowed from German'.

sources.citation: Efing, Christian. 2025. Jenisch – Sprache oder Soziolekt einer vergessenen Minderheit? Sprachreport 41(3): 1-11. Mannheim: IDS (whole issue PDF, DOI 10.14618/sr-3-2025-efi)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Section 'Aussprache und Schreibung' (p. 6): there is no specific 'Jenisch' pronunciation; pronunciation follows the speaker's own German/Swiss/Austrian dialect, and donor-language vocabulary (Romani, Yiddish) is phonetically-phonologically fully adapted to the regional surrounding language. Nothing on stress/accent as such.

sources.citation: Matras, Yaron. 2013. Jenisch. In G. Khan (ed.), Encyclopedia of Hebrew Language and Linguistics, vol. 2, 383-384. Leiden: Brill (author's PDF)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Words of unknown origin 'adhere to German rules of word formation and phonology'; Hebrew items entered 'with the Ashkenazi pronunciation'. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Matras, Yaron. 2010. Jenisch. Manchester Language Contact case-study web page (last updated 11-10-2010), via the Internet Archive
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sociohistory, lexicon composition and five Unterdeufstetten example sentences; no phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Efing, Christian. 2005. Das Lützenhardter Jenisch. Studien zu einer deutschen Sondersprache (Sondersprachenforschung 11). Wiesbaden: Harrassowitz. 337 pp. (author's PDF, Univ. Wuppertal)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ch. VII.5.1-5.2 'Die schwäbische Mundart in Lützenhardt' / 'Phonetisch-phonologische Einflüsse' (pp. 148-152): no Rotwelsch-dialect Sondersprache has ever been shown to develop its own phonetic profile; it 'grundsätzlich die Lautung der sie umgebenden Hoch- oder Umgangssprache beziehungsweise des sie umgebenden Dialekts annimmt' (pp. 150-151); Lützenhardt Swabian sound features are applied consistently to the Jenisch vocabulary; 'Eigenständige, mundartunabhängige phonetisch-phonologische Besonderheiten im Lützenhardter Jenisch lassen sich kaum feststellen' (p. 152). Segmental only; no mention…

sources.citation: Roth, Hansjörg. 2005/2010. Jenisch. Historisches Lexikon der Schweiz (online)
sources.note: Vocabulary c. 600 basic words related to late-medieval Rotwelsch; speakers learn Jenisch 'gemäss ihrem regionalen Dialekt'; no phonology.

sources.citation: Efing, Christian. 2004. Jenisch unter Schaustellern. Mit einem Glossar aus schriftlichen Quellen (Sondersprachenforschung 10). Wiesbaden: Harrassowitz. 216 pp. (author's PDF; text layer is code-point-shifted, decoded copy saved)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Subsection 'Lautung' (ch. on Einfluß der Mundarten): the pronunciation of the Jenisch vocabulary of the one recorded Rhineland speaker is 'absolut identisch' with that of Rhenish dialect lexemes; Rotwelsch dialects adapt 'in Syntax, Wortbildung – und auch Lautung – etc. fast ausnahmslos der deutschen bzw. der jeweiligen regionalen Grammatik' (fn. in ch. I). No stress statement.

sources.citation: Matras, Yaron. 1998. The Romani element in German secret languages: Jenisch and Rotwelsch. In Y. Matras (ed.), The Romani element in non-standard speech, 193-230. Wiesbaden: Harrassowitz (author's scan, image-only; tesseract scanned at 300 dpi saved)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sect. 5 'Structural features of Romani items in non-standard German', p. 225: the donor Sinti-Manuš Romani itself has shifted to initial stress under German contact; among adaptation features of Romani items in the German-based secret varieties, 'A curious phonological feature is the word-final stress in katšém "pub", through preservation of the Romani stress (Rom. kacima) with loss of the final syllable.' Only this single-word remark; no general rule for Jenisch stress.

sources.citation: Wittich, Engelbert & L. Günther. 1915-1916. Die jenische Sprache. Archiv für Kriminal-Anthropologie und Kriminalistik 63: 1-46, 97-133, 372-396; 64/65: 127-183, 297-355 (archive.org scanned of vols 62-63 and 64-65, Univ. Michigan copies; vol. 66 (1917) 33-89 not on archive.org)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Günther's philological Vorbemerkung and Wittich's Einleitung (63: 22-25) plus the German-Jenisch wordlist; Wittich only notes he wrote the words following 'das schwäbische Idiom.. [und] mein Gehör' (p. 24-25). No statement on Betonung/Akzent (a full-text search for stress/accent both volumes: nothing relevant).
